skills.name: Study the graph of a quadratic function y = ax² + bx + c

note.text:
The graph of y = ax² + bx + c is a parabola.
• If a > 0 it is ∪-shaped and has a lowest point (minimum). If a < 0 it is ∩-shaped with a highest point (maximum).
• It crosses the y-axis at (0, c).
• It is symmetrical about the vertical line x = −b/2a, the axis of symmetry. The turning point is on this line.
• Completing the square gives the turning point: y = (x − h)² + k turns at (h, k).
To draw it: make a table of values, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve, not with straight lines.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to describe the parabola y = ax² + bx + c: its shape, y-intercept, axis of symmetry and turning point, and draw it from a table.
Builds on: Lesson {8} (completing the square) and Lesson {20} (drawing graphs from tables).
Leads to: Lessons {24} and {25} (the discriminant and solving quadratics with graphs).

sections.heading: The shape of a parabola
Reading the features
sections.text:
For y = ax² + bx + c:
• y-intercept: ({0}, c).
• axis of symmetry: x = −b/{2}a.
• turning point: put that x into the equation.
For y = {quad(1, -2, -3)}: c = {-3}; x = {2}/{2} = {1}; y = {1} − {2} − {3} = {-4}. So the minimum is ({1}, {-4}).
Completing the square gives the same answer: {quad(1, -2, -3)} = (x − {1})² − {4}.

the lowest or highest point of the parabola
the vertical line through the turning point

mistake.why: x = −b/{2}a with b = {-2}: −({-2})/{2} = {1}. The minus sign in the formula matters.

worked_example.problem: For y = {quad(1, b, c)}, find the y-intercept, the axis of symmetry and the turning point.
steps: Turning point: y at x = {-b / 2} is {(-b / 2) * (-b / 2) + b * (-b / 2) + c}. a = {1} > {0}, so it is a minimum.

cards.idea: The y-intercept of y = ax² + bx + c is c: put x = {0}.
The axis of symmetry is x = −b/{2}a; the turning point lies on it.

cards.idea: a > {0}: ∪ shape with a minimum. a < {0}: ∩ shape with a maximum.
example: y = {quad(-1, 4, 0)} is ∩-shaped: it has a maximum

The turning point is not the y-intercept. Put x = {h} into the equation.

solution: y at x = {h}: {s * h * h} + {br(-2 * s * h * h)} + {br(s * h * h + v)} = {v}.
a = {s} is {s > 0 ? 'positive: ∪ shape, minimum' : 'negative: ∩ shape, maximum'}.

That parabola turns at x = {-h}, the mirror image.
